phase3_findings.description: VC-66/VC-67 FAIL: changelog.d/351.fixed.md lines 8-10 state unconditionally that a result whose headers are too large, or whose table could not be built, produces a could-not-be-displayed text block; _format.py:349-370 emits it only when raw_rows and not last_sql_is_introspection (schema-lookup results and row-less frames get no block). Release note ships to users, so not behavior-inert (self-contradicting-diff carve-out).
Release note omits the schema-lookup (introspection) exception at _format.py:361; sentence is false for SHOW/catalog results whose headers are too large or whose table could not be built.

run_sql_display_line's broad except returns '' when _compute_table_payload raises, while the formatter replaces the table with 'could not be displayed' text; the agent is told nothing and may describe rows the user never sees (fails open on the PR's core promise).
'Agent told N == user table shows N' invariant lives in call sequence: _small_result_to_markdown or _trim_blocks_to_budget can change/drop the block after run_sql_display_line computed its line.

Table payload is an untyped dict; a TypedDict with NotRequired row_cap and a total_rows helper would remove duplicated row_count+truncated reconstructions in _format.py and the underscore-named cross-module seam.

fix_decisions.claim_text: run_sql_display_line returns empty on payload-build exception while user sees could-not-be-displayed
fix_decisions.evidence: AC12 mandates no display line when the display-line work raises
